items.topic: Axillary crutches — two-finger space under axilla; weight on handgrips not armpits
items.stem: The nurse fits axillary crutches for a client with a non-weight-bearing lower extremity injury. Which teaching point is correct?

options.text: Keep about two finger widths between the axilla and the crutch pad, and bear weight through the hands on the handgrips
Rest the axilla firmly on the crutch pads so the armpits carry most of the body weight
Adjust the crutches so the pads sit tightly against the armpits with no space
Hold both crutches in one hand and hop without using the handgrips

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: axillary crutch should be two fingers distant between axilla and pad; weight focused on hand grips, not armpits, to prevent axillary nerve damage. StatPearls: shoulder pad about 2 inches (2 finger widths) below axilla; do not rest axilla on shoulder pad (crutch palsy risk).
rationales.B: Incorrect. Resting weight on the axilla risks brachial plexus/crutch palsy; weight belongs on the hands.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both sources require space under the axilla, not a tight fit against the armpit.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Proper crutch gait uses handgrips with crutches positioned for support.

items.topic: Ostomy stoma — moist pink/red healthy; purple/black report promptly
items.stem: During colostomy pouch care, which stoma finding should the nurse report to the provider immediately?

options.text: A moist, dark pink to red stoma
A purple or black stoma
Mild postoperative stoma edema that is expected to shrink over weeks
A small amount of mucus on the stoma surface

rationales.A: Incorrect. OpenStax and MedlinePlus describe a healthy stoma as moist and pink or red.
rationales.B: Correct. OpenStax: bluish, purple, black, or pale stomas should be reported. MedlinePlus: contact the provider if the stoma turns purple, black, or white.
rationales.C: Incorrect. OpenStax/MedlinePlus note expected postoperative swelling that shrinks over weeks.
rationales.D: Incorrect. MedlinePlus notes mucus may be seen on a healthy stoma.

items.stem: A client has a new ileostomy. For each nursing action, specify whether it is Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Document that a moist pink-to-red stoma is an expected healthy finding
Notify the provider promptly if the stoma becomes purple or black
Reassure the client that a dry, pale stoma is preferred over a moist one
Ignore peristomal skin redness because leakage never irritates skin

items.topic: Mumps — Droplet + Standard precautions until 5 days after parotitis onset
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: An adolescent is admitted with mumps parotitis. Which isolation plan is appropriate?

options.text: Droplet plus Standard Precautions until 5 days after onset of parotid swelling
Airborne Precautions alone for 24 hours after antibiotics begin
Contact Precautions only, discontinued when fever resolves
No transmission-based precautions because mumps is not contagious after symptoms begin

rationales.A: Correct. CDC Appendix A: mumps Droplet + Standard until 5 days after onset of swelling. Merck: isolate 5 days from parotitis onset; CDC recommends standard and droplet precautions for 5 days after parotitis onset.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Mumps is managed with droplet, not airborne-only, precautions; antibiotics are not the keyed duration trigger.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Contact-only and fever resolution are not the CDC/Merck isolation standard for mumps.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Contagiousness continues around symptom onset; isolation for 5 days after swelling is required.

sources.evidence: Droplet + Standard until 5 days after onset of swelling.

items.topic: Nasogastric tube — verify placement by x-ray before initial use/feeding
items.stem: A nurse has just inserted a nasogastric feeding tube. What is the priority action before initiating the first feeding?

options.text: Verify tube placement with x-ray imaging before use
Begin the feeding immediately after feeling resistance during insertion
Rely only on air insufflation (whoosh test) without imaging
Clamp the tube for 24 hours before any verification

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: placement must be verified via x-ray imaging prior to use. Open RN Nursing Advanced Skills: placement must be verified immediately after insertion by an X-ray before use.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Resistance alone does not confirm gastric placement; feeding into a misplaced tube risks aspiration.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Open RN: air auscultation (whoosh) is unreliable and should no longer be used to verify placement.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Verification is needed before use; an arbitrary 24-hour delay without confirmation is unsafe.

items.topic: Glasgow Coma Scale — combined score < 8 typically indicates coma
items.stem: When interpreting the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) after head trauma, which statement is correct?

options.text: A combined score less than 8 is typically regarded as coma
The highest possible combined GCS score is 8
GCS scores are based only on pupil size, not eye/verbal/motor responses
A score of 15 always means the client requires immediate intubation

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: combined scores < 8 are typically regarded as coma. OpenStax: GCS score lower than 8 indicates problems with consciousness / monitor for increased ICP.
rationales.B: Incorrect. OpenStax: highest possible GCS score is 15.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both sources describe eye opening, verbal, and motor response components.
rationales.D: Incorrect. 15 is the maximum (least impaired) score; it does not itself mandate intubation.

items.topic: Cushing syndrome cues SATA — moon face, buffalo hump, truncal obesity, striae
items.stem: Which findings are characteristic of Cushing syndrome? Select all that apply.

options.text: Facial rounding (moon face)
Dorsal cervical fat pad (buffalo hump) with truncal obesity
Purplish abdominal striae
Diffuse bronze hyperpigmentation as the only expected skin change from primary adrenal failure
Central obesity with relatively slender extremities
Acute hypothermia with areflexia as the defining presentation

rationales.A: Correct. Merck and OpenStax describe moon face / facial rounding.
rationales.B: Correct. Merck: truncal obesity with dorsal cervical fat pads (buffalo hump). OpenStax: fatty deposits between the shoulders (buffalo hump).
rationales.C: Correct. Merck lists striae; OpenStax notes purplish striae.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Bronze hyperpigmentation is classic for primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison), not Cushing.
rationales.E: Correct. Merck: truncal obesity with slender distal extremities; OpenStax: central obesity with thin extremities.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Extreme hypothermia with areflexia describes myxedema coma, not Cushing.

items.topic: NGN bowtie — myxedema coma: IV thyroid hormone + glucocorticoids; hypothermia/respiratory depression
items.stem: A client with long-standing hypothyroidism presents unresponsive with severe hypothermia and hypoventilation. Complete the bowtie: most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Adrenal crisis from abrupt steroid withdrawal only

actions.text: Administer intravenous thyroid hormone (T4/T3) as ordered
Give glucocorticoids as ordered while adrenal insufficiency is not yet excluded
Rapidly rewarm with aggressive external heating to reverse hypotension
Start high-dose oral methimazole immediately as first-line therapy
Encourage ambulation without airway or temperature support

parameters.text: Serial peak flow only as the sole monitoring plan
Orthostatic blood pressure after sprint exercise
Urine specific gravity every minute without respiratory assessment

rationales.K1: Incorrect. Thyroid storm is a hyperthyroid emergency (hyperthermia/tachycardia), not hypothyroid coma.
rationales.K2: Correct. Merck/OpenStax: myxedema coma — life-threatening hypothyroidism with hypothermia, altered mentation, respiratory depression.
rationales.K3: Incorrect. While glucocorticoids are given because adrenal insufficiency cannot be excluded, the presentation described is myxedema coma.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. Serotonin syndrome is a toxidrome unrelated to this hypothyroid picture.
rationales.A1: Correct. Merck: treat with IV T4 (or T3); OpenStax: intravenous thyroid hormone replacement.
rationales.A2: Correct. Merck: glucocorticoids given because central hypothyroidism/adrenal insufficiency often cannot be initially excluded.
rationales.A3: Incorrect. Merck: do not rewarm rapidly — may precipitate hypotension or arrhythmias.
rationales.A4: Incorrect. Methimazole treats hyperthyroidism/thyroid storm, not myxedema coma.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. Supportive airway/temperature care is required; ambulation is not priority.
rationales.P1: Correct. Extreme hypothermia is characteristic; low-reading thermometers may be needed (Merck).
rationales.P2: Correct. Respiratory depression/CO2 retention and hypoxemia require ventilation/PaO2 monitoring (Merck/OpenStax).
rationales.P3: Incorrect. Peak flow alone does not address hypothermia/coma monitoring needs.
rationales.P4: Incorrect. Not a priority parameter in unresponsive hypothermic myxedema coma.

items.topic: Chest tube drainage — one-way system so air/fluid leave but cannot re-enter pleural space
items.stem: A client has a chest tube connected to a specialized drainage device after pneumothorax. What is the primary purpose of this drainage system design?

options.text: Allow air and fluid to leave the pleural space while preventing room air from flowing back in (one-way drainage)
Force room air into the pleural space to reinflate the lung
Replace the need for any occlusive dressing if the tube becomes dislodged
Eliminate the need to monitor respiratory status after insertion

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: drainage devices are designed for one-way drainage so air/fluids flow out but nothing flows back in. Merck: ambulatory devices connect to a one-way valve (e.g., Heimlich valve).
rationales.B: Incorrect. Re-entry of air into the pleural space would worsen pneumothorax.
rationales.C: Incorrect. OpenStax separately notes three-sided occlusive dressing readiness if a chest tube becomes dislodged; the canister design does not replace that emergency action.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Respiratory monitoring remains essential while a chest tube is in place.

sources.evidence: Specialized drainage device one-way: air/fluids out, nothing back in.

items.jurisdiction_note: CNO guidance and Canadian federal MAID framework; RNs/RPNs support but only NP/physician may administer MAID medications.
items.topic: Ontario MAID — RN/RPN may support care but cannot administer MAID medications
items.stem: An Ontario RN is assisting a nurse practitioner who is providing medical assistance in dying (MAID). Which action is within the RN’s legal role?

options.text: Insert an intravenous line with an order for later use by the NP/physician administering MAID medications
Personally administer the medications that will cause the client’s death
Independently determine MAID eligibility and write the MAID medication order
Pressure the client to choose MAID to free a hospital bed

rationales.A: Correct. CNO: RNs/RPNs may assist by activities such as inserting an IV line (with an order) that will be used to administer MAID medications; only NPs and physicians may administer those medications.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CNO: only NPs and physicians may administer medications to cause death for practitioner-assisted MAID; RNs/RPNs are not permitted to administer them.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Eligibility assessment/administration authority is limited to NPs and physicians.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CNO: nurses giving information must not encourage or pressure the client to choose MAID.

sources.title: Guidance on Nurses’ Roles in Medical Assistance in Dying
sources.evidence: RN/RPN may insert IV with order; only NP/physician administer MAID meds; no pressure.

items.jurisdiction_note: CNO conscientious objection rules for MAID participation.
items.topic: Ontario MAID conscientious objection — transfer care; continue unrelated care; do not convey objection to client
items.stem: An Ontario nurse conscientiously objects to participating in MAID for an assigned client. What is the correct next action?

options.text: Transfer care to another appropriate provider and continue other nursing care unrelated to MAID until replacement is arranged, without expressing moral judgment to the client
Tell the client that choosing MAID is morally wrong and refuse all care immediately
Abandon the client without arranging alternate care
Administer the MAID medications personally despite the objection

rationales.A: Correct. CNO: conscientious objection must not be directly conveyed to the patient; transfer care to another nurse/provider; continue other nursing care unrelated to MAID until a replacement is found.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Objection must not be conveyed; moral judgments about the client must not be expressed; unrelated care continues until transfer.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Care must be transferred appropriately; abandonment is not permitted.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Objection means the nurse does not provide/assist MAID activities; administration is also outside RN authority.

sources.title: Guidance on Nurses’ Roles in Medical Assistance in Dying
sources.evidence: Do not convey objection; transfer care; continue unrelated care until replacement.

items.topic: Neonatal phototherapy — diaper only + eye protection; monitor temperature
items.stem: The nurse prepares a term newborn for overhead phototherapy for hyperbilirubinemia. Which action is correct?

options.text: Place the infant under the lights wearing only a diaper with eye patches/mask in place, and monitor temperature frequently
Dress the infant in a heavy sleeper and leave the eyes uncovered for bonding under the lights
Cover the infant completely with blankets so no skin is exposed to the light
Skip temperature checks because phototherapy cannot affect body temperature

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: infant wears only a diaper and eye patches; monitor temperature every 2 hours because phototherapy can elevate temperature. Open RN: usually only a diaper; patches/mask protect eyes; monitor temperature frequently for overheating.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Clothing blocks light exposure; eyes require protection under phototherapy lights.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Maximal safe skin exposure (with genital/eye protection) is needed for effective phototherapy.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Both sources require temperature monitoring because of overheating risk.

items.topic: NGN matrix — phototherapy safety actions indicated vs not
items.stem: A newborn is receiving overhead phototherapy. For each action, specify Indicated or Not indicated.

rows.text: Keep eye patches or an opaque eye mask in place while under the lights
Expose maximal skin by using only a diaper (genital coverage)
Leave the eyes uncovered continuously under the lights to promote bonding

rationales.R1: Indicated. OpenStax/Open RN: eye patches/mask protect eyes during phototherapy.
rationales.R2: Indicated. Both sources: diaper only to maximize skin exposure.
rationales.R3: Indicated. Both sources: monitor temperature; phototherapy can overheat the infant.
rationales.R4: Not indicated. Eyes must be protected while under the lights; uncovering for feeding/assessment is timed, not continuous under lights.
